title.narrative: Strengthening Institutional Capacity of SAWEN to combat wildlife crime

description.narrative: The objective of the proposed IDF Grant is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the South Asia Wildlife Enforcement Network (SAWEN) and its Secretariat for coordinated and organized approaches to combat wildlife crime in South Asia. SAWEN is an intergovernmental body comprising eight countries of South Asia – Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka -- that is aimed at combating illegal wildlife trafficking in the region through coordinated and organized actions. There is an urgent need to strengthen SAWEN to enable to South Asian member counties to have a better understanding of issues that pertain with combating illegal wildlife crime and put in place mechanisms to address the gaps and areas of synergies in wildlife and trade legislations that could be creatively and effectively used to adopt legal measures at the regional level with the cooperation of different countries in South Asia. The capacity of the SAWEN Secretariat needs to be up-scaled to provide strong linkages among the member countries for effective coordination, information flow and enhancement of enforcement efforts along the border areas. This proposed IDF grant will provide the much needed momentum for SAWEN establishment and operational effectiveness. The development objective of the proposed IDF Grant is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the South Asia Wildlife Enforcement Network (SAWEN), through its Secretariat and its focal points in member countries for coordinated and organized approaches to combat wildlife crime in South Asia. SAWEN is an intergovernmental body comprising eight countries of South Asia - Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka -- that is aimed at combating illegal wildlife trafficking in the region through coordinated and organized actions.There is an urgent need to strengthen SAWEN to enable South Asian member counties to have (i) a better understanding of issues that pertain to combating illegal wildlife crime, (ii) put in place mechanisms to address the knowledge and capacity gaps, and (iii) build on areas of synergies in wildlife and trade legislation that could be creatively andeffectively used to adopt legal measures at the regional level with the cooperation of SAWEN member countries. The capacity of the SAWEN Secretariat needs to be up-scaled to provide strong linkages among the SAWEN focal points in member countries for effective coordination, information flow and enhancement of enforcement efforts within each country and along the border areas. This proposed IDF grant will provide the much needed momentum for SAWEN's formal establishment and operational effectiveness.
